entries.name: Product of experts
entries.definition: A probabilistic model family that combines expert factors over the same observations by multiplying their values and normalizing the product over the observation space.
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes the general normalized-product construction, including latent-variable experts, rather than an arithmetic mixture, a training algorithm or a language-model-specific factorization. The original cooperative-learning setting does not require experts to be separately trained. AIO FactorizedLLM has Product of experts as a related synonym, but its definition and parent restrict it to large language models; that related synonym does not identify the general family. Logarithmic opinion pooling uses normalized exponent weights and has a separate aggregation scope. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 373 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared. The sole normalized hit is Product of experts as a related synonym of FactorizedLLM; its language-specific definition and parent distinguish it from the generic candidate. Both full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files and returned 59 lines each. All 29 unique matched contents were read; other hits concern citations, training components, prior boundary discussions or pending leads. All 88 semantic label/synonym hits, 20 exact fully annotated AIO nodes with outgoing edges, their generated records and four complete native neighbors were inspected or verified unchanged after previous full reading. Absence is bounded to this pin and inspected semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The normalizer must be finite and positive. Continuous expert densities being individually normalized does not alone guarantee that their product is integrable; nonoverlapping supports can also make normalization impossible.

Tractable inference within each expert does not make the product normalizer, model sampling or likelihood learning automatically tractable. Exact likelihood derivatives involve the full product distribution; short-chain CD is a distinct approximate learning procedure.

Experts need not use disjoint input dimensions, be individually well fitted, or produce a sharper or better calibrated distribution in every setting. A product of Gaussian factors remains Gaussian when well defined, so Gaussian factors alone do not represent arbitrary multimodality.

Conditional independence is between separate latent expert states given all modeled observations. Missing observations can couple the experts. The original architecture is not defined by a sparse router or an arithmetic average of expert predictions.

Unit exponent products and geometric opinion averages are not interchangeable: multiplying duplicate factors can sharpen a distribution, while identical distributions pooled with exponent weights summing to one remain unchanged. No empirical advantage or author implementation is certified.

claims.statement: For observations x, form p(x)=product_m f_m(x;theta_m)/Z(theta), with Z the sum or integral of the product over x and 0<Z<infinity. Expert factors may be unnormalized; multiplying one by a positive x-independent constant cancels in the final normalization. For parameters local to expert m, the exact log-likelihood derivative is its log-factor derivative at the data minus the expectation of that derivative under the full product model. In the latent-expert construction, f_m(x)=sum_hm f_m(x,h_m), and separate expert hidden variables are conditionally independent given a completely observed x, allowing separate inference when each expert is tractable. This does not imply independence of observed coordinates or independence of experts after some observations are marginalized. Restricted Boltzmann machines instantiate the family with one expert per hidden unit, whereas product HMMs use complete HMM sequence distributions as factors.

entries.name: Product of hidden Markov models
entries.definition: A sequence-model family that multiplies the marginal probabilities assigned to a complete observation sequence by several hidden Markov models and normalizes the product over sequences of the same length.
entries.identity_notes: PoHMM is Brown and Hinton’s undirected product construction with one hidden chain per expert. It is not a mixture that selects one HMM, an ordinary single-chain HMM, or a directed factorial HMM whose multiple latent chains jointly generate locally normalized emissions. Taylor and Hinton’s later AIS study retains this model identity and supplies an evaluation procedure, not a new synonymous architecture. The model is not restricted to linguistic sequences. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 373 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared. The sole normalized hit is Product of experts as a related synonym of FactorizedLLM; its language-specific definition and parent distinguish it from the generic candidate. Both full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files and returned 59 lines each. All 29 unique matched contents were read; other hits concern citations, training components, prior boundary discussions or pending leads. All 88 semantic label/synonym hits, 20 exact fully annotated AIO nodes with outgoing edges, their generated records and four complete native neighbors were inspected or verified unchanged after previous full reading. Absence is bounded to this pin and inspected semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The partition function depends on model parameters and sequence length. Separate forward–backward computations evaluate the unnormalized product and complete-data hidden posteriors; they do not by themselves give the product’s global normalizer or exact likelihood. Small finite models can be enumerated, but this does not establish scalable tractability.

When observations are missing or future observations are integrated out, the experts can become dependent. Exact separate posterior inference given a complete sequence is not a claim of equally simple causal prediction from a prefix.

CD learning is approximate, and the customary short-chain update is not generally an exact likelihood or contrastive-objective gradient. The Brown paper’s initial pseudocode writes probability derivatives where its final update uses log derivatives; this record follows the log-score update supported by the later explicit formulation.

Brown Equation (3) places a derivative outside a posterior expectation. The score identity used here means the expectation of the log-joint derivative at the current posterior, without differentiating through that posterior. The shared deterministic emission-feature extension is optional, not an extra required stochastic latent layer.

Taylor Section 3.3 estimates normalization with an AIS path that tempers emission potentials inside hidden-path sums. This is generally different from simply raising whole HMM marginal likelihoods to fractional powers. Approximate normalizer estimates, and their logarithms, are not exact log likelihoods or a universal reliability guarantee.
The papers’ language, rainfall and dance examples do not establish universal superiority. No author code, training experiment or AIS implementation was reproduced.

claims.statement: For fixed length T, let p_m(v_1:T) sum each expert HMM’s joint probability over its hidden paths. Define p(v_1:T)=product_m p_m(v_1:T)/Z_T. Given the entire observed sequence, infer each expert’s hidden path posterior separately with forward–backward. A blocked Gibbs transition samples one path from each such posterior, then independently at each time samples an observation from the normalized product of the emissions selected by those paths. For CD-k learning, contrast each expert’s log-marginal score on the data and on the k-step reconstruction, treating reconstructed observations as fixed in the customary update. Each score is the posterior expectation of the derivative of the HMM log joint, with that posterior held fixed for this identity; it is not the total derivative through the posterior of an expected log joint. Global normalization over sequences distinguishes the model from independently normalizing a product emission at every time while retaining independent hidden-chain priors.

entries.name: Logarithmic opinion pool
entries.definition: A probability-aggregation method that forms a normalized weighted geometric mean of expert distributions over the same outcomes, using nonnegative exponent weights that sum to one.
entries.identity_notes: This record uses the normalized-weight convention inspected in Heskes and Hinton. It combines probability assessments, possibly conditional on an input, rather than spatially pooling neural activations. It is distinct from a linear opinion pool, a unit-exponent product learned cooperatively, and a particular algorithm for estimating the exponent weights. Broader log-linear combinations without the sum-to-one constraint require separate qualifications. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 373 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared. The sole normalized hit is Product of experts as a related synonym of FactorizedLLM; its language-specific definition and parent distinguish it from the generic candidate. Both full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files and returned 59 lines each. All 29 unique matched contents were read; other hits concern citations, training components, prior boundary discussions or pending leads. All 88 semantic label/synonym hits, 20 exact fully annotated AIO nodes with outgoing edges, their generated records and four complete native neighbors were inspected or verified unchanged after previous full reading. Absence is bounded to this pin and inspected semantic neighborhood.
limitations: An outcome assigned zero probability by any positively weighted expert receives zero pooled probability. Disjoint positively weighted supports can yield Z=0. Zero-weight experts are excluded from this veto; finite-divergence identities require compatible support.

The weighted-average KL bound is not a guarantee of improvement over every expert, calibrated uncertainty or empirical predictive superiority. It depends on nonnegative weights summing to one, and does not transfer unchanged to arbitrary unit-exponent products.

Pooling does not specify how expert models or their weights are trained. Heskes’s quadratic weight-selection objective is an approximation obtained by neglecting KL asymmetry terms for nearby distributions; it is not the exact general weight-optimization objective. Finite-data divergence estimates may be biased by fitting and overfitting.

The Heskes display following Equation (3) prints ambiguity A as positive log Z, conflicting with its nonnegative weighted-KL definition and the preceding prose. The consistent identity is A=-log Z. The normalization constraint there also integrates over x where conditional normalization requires y; these display slips are not adopted.

The variance example on printed p.270 reverses the precision ratio for the displayed KL argument order. The record relies on the probability-pool definition and the equal-variance example, not that reversed formula. No general weight-selection implementation or empirical result is certified.

claims.statement: For each input x, aggregate expert probabilities as pbar(y|x)=product_m p_m(y|x)^w_m/Z(x), with w_m>=0 and sum_m w_m=1. Omit zero-weight factors, and require 0<Z(x)<infinity. On a common support where the divergences are finite, pbar minimizes sum_m w_m KL(r||p_m) over normalized r, with the candidate r in the first KL argument. For a target distribution q, KL(q||pbar)=sum_m w_m KL(q||p_m)-sum_m w_m KL(pbar||p_m); the subtracted term is -log Z at a fixed input, or its expectation over inputs. Thus the pool is no worse in that KL direction than the weighted average of experts, not necessarily the best expert. A common likelihood update commutes with pooling when the same fixed normalized weights are retained and normalization exists. For binary logistic probabilities this rule averages logits; for equal-variance Gaussian experts it averages means while preserving that shared variance.

brown2001.reading_notes: All eight pages visually read. Publisher PMLR R3 reissue has no printed page numbers; catalog pp.21–28 differs from the original pp.3–11 cited in Hinton and Taylor. Equations1–2 define a normalized product of complete HMM sequence marginal probabilities, with a length-dependent partition function. Conditional on the complete visible sequence, hidden chains are independent and separately forward–backward tractable. Sampling hidden paths then normalized product emissions gives blocked Gibbs. CD uses data versus reconstruction log scores. Initial pseudocode probability derivatives and Equation3 derivative-outside-posterior-expectation notation need the qualifications saved in the record: expectation of score with fixed posterior, not differentiation through posterior weights. Section3.1 expressly distinguishes exact missing-symbol conditional scoring from prefix prediction. Section4 is an optional deterministic linear-feature/softmax emission factorization. Small symbolic experiments are not generalized performance evidence.

The display afterEq3 incorrectly prints A=positive logZ despite its weighted nonnegative KL definition and preceding minus-log prose; correct A=-logZ. The same paragraph integrates dx instead of dy in conditional normalization. Section3 Gaussian variance example reverses the precision ratio for its displayed KL direction. These display slips are not adopted. Eq5 quadratic weight objective drops KL-asymmetry terms and is generally approximate, exact for the equal-variance Gaussian example. native_neighbors.name: Sparse additive generative model
native_neighbors.definition: A generative model family for categorical text data that forms word probabilities by normalizing a background log-frequency vector plus sparse component deviations, allowing multiple generative facets to combine additively in log space.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: SAGE here denotes Eisenstein, Ahmed and Xing’s sparse additive generative construction, not Sage mathematical software or graph-neural aggregation. Its classification, topic and multifaceted uses share this parameterization; it is not synonymous with all naive Bayes models, sparse dictionary learning, sparse topic proportions or an arithmetic mixture of component word distributions. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 352 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; worktree returned 15 lines and main 19. All 16 unique matched contents were read: DocNADE contrasts, frontier and review references, plus four ignored-environment Sage/Pygments entries unrelated to AI SAGE. Twenty-one exact AIO nodes and four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Sparsity concerns log deviations. Finite logits still give positive word probabilities, and even zero-deviation words can change absolute probability through normalization; their relative odds remain those of the background when their deviations agree.

Additive log facets yield multiplicative unnormalized effects, not an arithmetic probability mixture. The model family does not require every document to have a single observed class or prohibit latent variables.

The Jeffreys-prior paragraph on PDF p.4 prints expected inverse variance equal to eta squared. Its preceding Gamma moment and b=eta squared/(a-1) instead give 1/eta squared for nonzero eta, with a>1 and positive scale. The printed final identity is not adopted; zero deviations require a limiting/numerical treatment. The improper prior is not represented as a normalized marginal distribution.

The paper warns that warm-starting tightly coupled deviation/variance updates can lock in early sparsity patterns. Neither approximate inference nor Newton updates establish global convergence or calibrated posterior uncertainty.

The single-component rank-one Hessian argument is not asserted unchanged for sums over multiple facet combinations. No author implementation, universal predictive advantage or numerical benchmark result is certified.

claims.statement: For a component k, set p(w=i|k) proportional to exp(m_i+eta_ki), normalizing over the vocabulary. Multiple selected facets contribute a sum of their deviation vectors before this normalization; no additional token-level switch is needed to choose which facet generates the word. This does not remove latent topic assignments used by a topic-model variant. The paper places sparsity-inducing priors on deviations, using zero-mean Gaussian components with latent variances: an exponential variance prior gives a Laplace marginal, while an alternative improper Jeffreys prior gives a different shrinkage construction. It combines MAP estimates of deviations with variational treatment of other latent quantities. For a single component and fixed expected precisions, the gradient is observed or expected counts minus total count times word probabilities minus the precision-weighted deviations; its Hessian is a rank-one term minus a diagonal term, enabling the reported efficient Newton update.

native_neighbors.name: Mixture density network
native_neighbors.definition: A neural conditional-density architecture whose input-dependent outputs parameterize the mixing weights and component distributions of a finite mixture over target variables.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is Bishop’s combined neural-network and mixture-density construction. It predicts a conditional distribution, not only a conditional mean, and does not require the output density to be unimodal. The report’s worked model uses a feed-forward network and isotropic Gaussian components; other component families or covariance parameterizations are choices within the broader construction. It is distinct from an unconditional fitted Gaussian mixture, a generic feed-forward classifier and a sparse mixture-of-experts large language model. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 349 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 5 and 5 lines respectively. All 3 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: the prior NADE-variant lead, RNADE source URL and previous review exclusion, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. limitations: Exponentiation makes the scale positive for finite real outputs but does not bound it away from zero or prevent likelihood concentration as a component scale approaches zero. The report’s wording about avoiding zero-variance pathologies is interpreted with this mathematical qualification.

The report sometimes calls sigma a variance, but Equation (23) uses sigma as a standard deviation. Its displayed population Equation (40) omits the negative sign required by the preceding negative-log-likelihood objective; Equations (43) and (47) omit dimension factors if read as general isotropic multivariate scale and total variance formulas. Those printed formulas are not adopted as general identities.
A mixture’s global mode generally requires optimization. Selecting a component center by peak height or weight is an approximation under separation assumptions, not an exact general mode calculation.

A finite architecture and local optimization do not establish an arbitrary-accuracy fit, calibrated uncertainty, successful generalization or global optimality. The network models p(t|x), not p(x), unless an additional input model is provided.
No author implementation, later experimental pages or general approximation theorem was audited; finite curator calculations check only the displayed cases.

claims.statement: For input x, a neural network outputs parameters defining p(t|x)=sum_i alpha_i(x) phi_i(t|x). In the report’s c-dimensional isotropic Gaussian construction, softmax outputs give nonnegative mixing weights summing to one, direct outputs give component means, and exponentiated outputs give positive standard deviations sigma_i, with covariance sigma_i squared times the identity. The mixture can have dependent target coordinates even though coordinates are independent within each isotropic component. Minimize the sum of negative log mixture densities over input/target pairs. With responsibilities r_i=alpha_i phi_i/p(t|x), the output-logit derivative of one negative log likelihood is alpha_i-r_i; the mean derivative is r_i(mu_i-t)/sigma_i squared and the log-scale derivative is r_i(c-||t-mu_i|| squared/sigma_i squared). Backpropagate these derivatives through the network. Mixture weights are conditional component priors before observing t; responsibilities condition on both x and t. The conditional mean is the weighted mean of component centers and need not be a mode or a plausible branch of a multivalued inverse mapping.

native_neighbors.name: Contrastive divergence
native_neighbors.definition: A parameter-learning algorithm for energy-based or product-of-experts models that replaces the equilibrium negative-phase expectation by configurations obtained from a short model-invariant Markov chain restarted at observed data, without differentiating through the chain distribution.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes the customary contrastive-divergence update family, including CD-1 and CD-k, rather than only the formal difference-of-KL-divergences objective that motivated it. The number of transition steps is an algorithm parameter, not a separate architecture. It differs from persistent-chain learning, CD-PercLoss prediction search and pairwise representation-learning losses. The short aliases are contextual, not evidence of equivalence to every use of those initials. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 370 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files throughout both worktree and main, returning 29 lines each; all 22 unique matched contents were read. Hits described CD as a training component, a pending lead or a boundary from CD-PercLoss, not an existing candidate record. All 61 semantic label/synonym hits, 21 exact annotated AIO nodes with outgoing edges, corresponding generated records and four native neighbors were inspected. Previously fully read contextual files were verified byte-identical. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and inspected neighborhood.
limitations: A short-chain CD estimate is generally biased for the likelihood gradient and is not generally the exact negative gradient of the formal contrastive-divergence objective. A small objective or accurate reconstruction can coexist with poor global modeling when the chain mixes slowly.

The binary-RBM CD-1 field can have unequal cross partial derivatives, so it is not universally the gradient of any scalar objective. The inspected convergence paper also constructs cycling with a particular nonconvex regularizer; this is not a claim that ordinary L2-regularized CD always cycles. Existence of a regularized fixed point does not establish convergence to it.

Exact Gibbs transitions require sampled states. Conditional expectations can replace final sufficient statistics by Rao–Blackwellization, but feeding probability-valued states into later nonlinear transition conditionals defines a different approximation. Hinton Section 8 explicitly uses such a probability-valued visible reconstruction in its digit experiment; that variant is not silently equated to exact binary Gibbs CD.

The original simulations do not prove universal likelihood improvement, unbiased learning or global convergence. Their digit classification experiments also disclose test-set model selection; no reported ranking is adopted as a general property.

The algorithm is not tied to an RBM architecture, and the formal objective is not merely a difference of mean log likelihoods: distribution-entropy terms matter. No author implementation, training run or complete convergence theorem is certified.

claims.statement: For each observed example or minibatch, initialize a Markov chain at the data and perform k transitions with the model parameters held fixed. For an RBM, alternate sampled hidden and visible blocks, then compute hidden conditional expectations at the resulting visible configurations for the negative statistics. Update weights by a learning rate times observed-data minus k-step reconstructed visible-hidden statistics; update biases by the corresponding first-moment differences. More generally, contrast derivatives of the unnormalized log model at the data and chain endpoints, treating the endpoints as fixed for the update. The motivating objective is C_k(theta)=KL(q_data||p_theta)-KL(q_data T_theta^k||p_theta). Its exact derivative also contains the parameter dependence of the k-step distribution; the customary CD update omits that contribution. With a fixed ergodic kernel and sufficiently long chains, the negative expectation approaches the equilibrium expectation; a short-chain update does not assume that limit has been reached.

evidence.locator: Sections 2–3, Equations (2.1)–(3.4), printed pp.1772–1777 / PDF pp.2–7; RBM specialization, Section 7, pp.1780–1782 / PDF pp.10–12; approximation analysis, Section 10, pp.1788–1791 / PDF pp.18–21

claims.statement: For the noiseless binary-RBM CD-1 update, the inspected source gives a one-visible/one-hidden counterexample with hidden bias fixed at zero and data visible=0.
